# COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (CAP) TREATED WITH ORAL ANTIBIOTICS

Empirical regimens listed here cover the usual pathogens associated with CAP, including atypical pathogens. Specific therapy should be guided by culture results.

## Diagnosis

Use the CAP Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) to assist with level of care decision
CAP Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) Calculator

---

References:

- Metlay JP, Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2019, 200(7):e45
- Sanford: Community Acquired Pneumonia
- Up-to-date website
Therapy:
## Previously healthy patients (i.e. no comorbidities):

(WITHOUT chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, renal failure, congestive heart failure, malignancy, alcoholism, asplenia, immunosuppressing conditions, or use of immunosuppressing drugs)
Preferred:
Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h [DI] for 5 days
< OR >
Amoxicillin 1000 mg PO q8h [R] for 5 days

## Patients with comorbidities:

(WITH chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diabetes, renal failure, congestive heart failure, malignancy, alcoholism, asplenia, immunosuppressing conditions or use of immunosuppressing drugs)
Preferred:
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO Q12H [R] for 5 days <AND> azithromycin po once on day 1, then 250 mg PO QDAY for 4 days [M]
< OR >
Cefdinir 300 mg PO Q12H [R] for 5 days <AND> azithromycin once on day 1, then 250 mg PO QDAY for 4 days [M]
< OR >
Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO Q12H [R] for 5 days <AND> doxycycline 100 mg PO Q12H for 5 days [DI]
< OR >
Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h [R] for 5 days <AND> doxycycline 100 mg PO Q12H for 5 days [DI]

## Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](beta-lactam-allergy-assessment)
Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h [DI] for 5 days
